headline.headline: SOX EXPLODE FOR SEVEN IN THIRD, BATTER ORIOLES, 9-3
headline.deck: Montgomery's 21st homer keys a stunning inning that buried Baltimore at Camden Yards
headline.body:
BALTIMORE — The Chicago White Sox turned a tied ballgame into a rout with a seven-run third inning Tuesday night, stunning the Baltimore Orioles 9-3 before an announced crowd of 17,581 at Camden Yards. The big inning, erupting out of a 1-1 tie through two frames, effectively ended the contest before the fourth inning began.

Colton Montgomery supplied the signature blow of the rally, launching his 21st home run of the season during the third-inning barrage. Salvador Perez added his second homer of the year to pad the lead, and the White Sox collected doubles from Andrew Benintendi, Gonzalez, and others to keep the Orioles' pitching staff in shambles. Baltimore managed only a Gunnar Henderson double and a Beavers two-bagger among its modest offensive contributions in the loss.

Chicago left 12 runners on base yet still rolled to a comfortable final margin, which underscored just how thoroughly the third inning carried the load. Baltimore scored twice in the fifth to trim the margin slightly, but the White Sox answered any threat with zeroes the rest of the way, finishing the game in 2 hours and 47 minutes. The Orioles, who entered the night trying to protect their standing in a competitive AL East, instead absorbed a lopsided defeat that left little room for optimism.

secondary.headline: METS SILENCE BLUE JAYS, 3-0, TO CLAIM SERIES IN TORONTO
secondary.deck: Alvarez and Torrens homer as New York wins three-game set with steady pitching
secondary.body:
TORONTO — The New York Mets scratched out single runs in the fifth, seventh, and ninth innings Tuesday, shutting out the Toronto Blue Jays 3-0 at Rogers Centre to claim the three-game series. Francisco Alvarez hit his ninth home run of the season and Luis Torrens added his second to supply the offensive punch in a tidy 2-hour, 38-minute contest before 41,538 fans.

New York's pitching staff was equally disciplined, holding Toronto scoreless across nine innings in a performance that belied the Mets' fifth-place standing in the NL East at 36-50. The Blue Jays, sitting at 40-46 in the AL East, wasted a noisy home crowd and fell further from contention in the process. Baty and Varsho each contributed doubles for New York, while Toronto struggled to generate any sustained threat against the Mets' bullpen.

secondary.headline: RANGERS RALLY PAST GUARDIANS, 4-2, IN AL CENTRAL TUSSLE
secondary.deck: Texas overcomes early two-run deficit with late-inning runs to escape Cleveland
secondary.body:
CLEVELAND — Cleveland scored twice in the first inning and appeared to have the upper hand, but the Texas Rangers answered with two runs in the third and added one apiece in the seventh and eighth to defeat the Guardians 4-2 before 21,674 at Progressive Field. The game was completed in a crisp 2 hours and 12 minutes.

The Rangers refused to let Cleveland's early lead stand, chipping away with methodical offense after the Guardians went quiet following their first-inning burst. Texas left only four runners on base, a sign of efficient clutch hitting that proved to be the difference. The Guardians, meanwhile, could not add to their early advantage and dropped a game they led wire to wire through only the first frame.

secondary.headline: PHILLIES ROLL, 8-0, AS BIDOIS SHINES AND PIRATES FALL FLAT
secondary.deck: Philadelphia erupts for six runs in seventh and eighth innings to rout Pittsburgh
secondary.body:
PHILADELPHIA — Starter Bidois earned the win and the Philadelphia Phillies cruised past the Pittsburgh Pirates 8-0 before a spirited Citizens Bank Park crowd of 41,710 on Tuesday night. The game was scoreless until the second inning, when the Phillies pushed across two runs, then Pittsburgh's pitching held until a three-run seventh and a three-run eighth blew the game open completely.

The Pirates never dented the scoreboard across nine innings, managing no answer to Philadelphia's dominant performance. J.T. Realmuto was hit by a pitch from Pittsburgh's Chandler during the game, adding a physical edge to the evening. Pittsburgh, struggling to find traction in the NL Central, was thoroughly outclassed in Citizens Bank Park, where the announced attendance of 41,710 witnessed one of the more complete team efforts of the Phillies' season.

column.headline: THOSE WHITE SOX ARE NO LONGER EASY TO IGNORE
column.body:
Nobody penciled the Chicago White Sox into anyone's October plans a few months ago, and plenty of observers around this league would still rather change the subject than discuss what is happening on the South Side. But seven runs in one inning, on the road, against a Baltimore club that fancied itself a contender? That is not a fluke. That is a team with teeth, and Colton Montgomery's 21st home run before the midpoint of the season is the kind of production that forces a reckoning.

Sal Perez, Benintendi, the whole crew in those road grays — they left 12 men on base and still won by six. Think about that. The Orioles had every reason to feel relief when Chicago stranded runner after runner, and instead Baltimore's night ended with another lopsided line in the loss column. When a team this deep into a rebuild starts doing this kind of damage in late June, the rest of the American League would be wise to stop assuming it knows how this story ends.

story.headline: TIGERS TORCH YANKEES, 9-3, BEHIND FOUR-HOMER ASSAULT AT THE STADIUM
story.deck: Detroit erupts early, often to hand New York its latest skid-extending loss
story.body:
NEW YORK — The Detroit Tigers rolled into Yankee Stadium and left no doubt, pounding out nine runs on the strength of four home runs to rout the home team 9-3 on Monday before 37,211 fans. Matt Vierling Carpenter got things started immediately, as Detroit plated four runs in the very first inning to seize control before New York could find its footing. The Tigers never looked back, adding two more in the third and three in the sixth to turn the contest into a rout.

Parker Meadows Kerry Carpenter launched his 13th home run of the season as part of that first-inning burst, and Riley Greene added his 11th later in the game. Spencer Torkelson chipped in his 14th, and Josh Outman contributed a blast as well, giving Detroit a murderers row of long-ball damage that the Yankees bullpen had no answer for. The only blemish for the Tigers came when Trey Sweeney Schuemann was hit by a pitch from Detroit starter Tarik Skubal, but the afternoon belonged overwhelmingly to the visitors.

For New York, Jim Rice launched his team-leading 23rd home run of the year, a solo shot that provided little consolation in a lopsided defeat. The Yankees entered the game sitting second in the AL East at 48-37 but have now dropped a string of consecutive contests, leaving the clubhouse searching for answers heading into the July stretch run. Detroit, meanwhile, collected the victory despite leaving 11 runners on base, a sign the offense had plenty more to give had the game remained competitive.

story.headline: ROCKETS REEL IN BOGDANOVIC AS NBA FREE AGENCY MARKET EXPLODES TO LIFE
story.deck: Houston lands sharpshooter on one-year deal while Philadelphia locks up Dean Wade for four years.
story.body:
The Houston Rockets wasted no time making their mark on the 2026 NBA free agency period, agreeing to a one-year deal with versatile shooting guard Bogdan Bogdanovic, sources confirmed to ESPN on Tuesday. The Serbian sharpshooter, known for his ability to create his own shot off the dribble and knock down clutch perimeter jumpers, gives Houston another offensive weapon to complement a young core hungry to push deeper into the postseason. Terms of the deal were not immediately disclosed, but the signing signals the Rockets' clear intention to compete now rather than wait.

Meanwhile, the Philadelphia 76ers shored up their frontcourt by landing forward Dean Wade on a four-year, $39 million contract, sources told ESPN. Wade, a versatile 6-foot-9 forward capable of defending multiple positions and spacing the floor with his shooting, fills a significant positional need for a Philadelphia squad still searching for the right supporting cast around its cornerstone pieces. The four-year commitment reflects the organization's belief that Wade's two-way skill set translates directly into their system.

Beyond the confirmed signings, the broader free agency landscape remains electric with speculation surrounding marquee names including LeBron James, Kawhi Leonard and Keon Ellis, whose next destinations could reshape the Western Conference picture entirely. Adding another layer of intrigue to the basketball world, the NBA confirmed it has received finalized bids exceeding $1 billion from more than 20 groups competing for spots in a proposed NBA Europe league, a development that underscores the sport's rapidly expanding global footprint as the calendar turns to July.

story.headline: WERENSKI PULLS PLUG ON DALLAS DEAL AS GREER, GRITSYUK FIND NEW HOMES
story.deck: Blue Jackets defenseman vetoes Stars trade while Ducks and Devils lock up key forwards
story.body:
Columbus Blue Jackets defenseman Zach Werenski has vetoed a proposed trade to the Dallas Stars, an NHL source confirmed Wednesday, dealing a significant blow to a Dallas club that had been pursuing the offensive blueliner to bolster its postseason push. Werenski, who holds a no-trade clause, exercised that right rather than relocate to Texas, leaving the Stars scrambling for defensive reinforcements on one of the busiest days of the NHL offseason calendar.

While the Werenski drama unfolded in Columbus, the Anaheim Ducks wasted no time adding Stanley Cup pedigree to their rising roster, signing forward AJ Greer to a four-year contract carrying an average annual value of $4.25 million. Greer, a physical winger with championship experience, fits the hard-nosed identity that Anaheim general manager Pat Verbeek has been constructing around a young core that scouts around the league increasingly regard as a legitimate future contender.

In Newark, the New Jersey Devils secured one of their most intriguing young forwards, locking up restricted free agent winger Arseny Gritsyuk on a three-year deal. Gritsyuk, who flashed dynamic offensive instincts during stretches of last season, gives the Devils another skilled piece alongside Nico Hischier and Jack Hughes as New Jersey continues building toward what the organization hopes will be a sustained championship window.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS NFL TEAMS RESHAPE ROSTERS FOR 2026
story.deck: Several franchises are making bold moves at quarterback as the league's offseason heats up.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has erupted into one of the most active roster-reshaping periods in recent memory, with quarterback movement dominating headlines from coast to coast. The Las Vegas Raiders completed a blockbuster trade this week, sending a package of draft picks to the Cleveland Browns in exchange for Deshaun Watson, who is expected to revitalize a Raiders offense that sputtered badly during the 2025 season. Meanwhile, the New Orleans Saints have emerged as serious suitors for veteran free agent Russell Wilson, whose one-year stint with the Pittsburgh Steelers ended without a postseason appearance.

The 2026 NFL Draft, held last month in Detroit, continues to generate debate among front offices and analysts alike. Colorado quarterback Shedeur Sanders, selected fifth overall by the Jacksonville Jaguars, has already begun working with the team's new offensive coordinator, and head coach Liam Coen has publicly expressed confidence that Sanders can start by Week 1. The Tennessee Titans, who held the top overall pick, selected Colorado wide receiver Travis Hunter, signaling a commitment to rebuilding their offensive skill positions around young talent.

On the free agency front, left tackle Trent Brown re-signed with the New England Patriots on a two-year deal, giving the rebuilt offense a veteran anchor up front. The Dallas Cowboys quietly parted ways with linebacker Micah Parsons, restructuring their defensive scheme under new coordinator Brian Johnson. Parsons, a four-time Pro Bowl selection, drew immediate interest from at least six teams before agreeing to terms with the Philadelphia Eagles, setting up what promises to be a fierce divisional rivalry with his former club.
